key_insight: SHROM builds an invertible, low-dimensional latent space for droplet shapes by combining shape-aware representation, neighbor-graph regularization, and an autoencoder.
engineering_relevance: This gives CFD and experimentalists a way to compress, compare, and interpolate fluid-interface morphologies across a design envelope without rerunning expensive breakup experiments.
method: Represent droplet contours with square-root velocity functions to encode shape robustly.
Construct a neighbor graph in shape space and regularize the autoencoder so latent neighbors preserve shape neighbors.
Train an invertible reduced-order model that reconstructs contours while keeping latent coordinates meaningful for clustering and interpolation.
evidence_signal: The study uses 301,539 inkjet droplet contours plus four breakup videos; the graph term boosts latent clustering ARI from 0.063 ± 0.059 to 0.781 ± 0.049, while waveform parameters predict full contours with R² = 0.878 ± 0.026.
watch_item: The model struggles across topology changes: no regularized latent captures both single-component and post-breakup shapes, and interpolation remains limited by reconstruction error.
paper_title: A shape-similarity latent space for fluid interfaces: invertible reduced-order modelling of droplet morphology
